template.name: Game Development
template.summary: 40 questions to align play, scope, production and release.

resolutionStates.label: Confirmed
resolutionStates.description: Use this as an accepted project premise.

resolutionStates.label: Provisional
resolutionStates.description: Use this for now, but keep it visibly open to revision.

resolutionStates.label: Not decided
resolutionStates.description: Leave this open. Do not let an AI silently fill it in.

resolutionStates.label: Ask for a proposal
resolutionStates.description: Request alternatives or a recommendation without treating one as chosen.

resolutionStates.label: Delegate within bounds
resolutionStates.description: Allow the implementer or AI to decide within the stated limits and report the choice.

resolutionStates.label: Does not apply
resolutionStates.description: Mark this question as outside the project.

messages.validation.provenanceRequired: Choose whose perspective this answer represents and who recorded it.
messages.validation.speakingRoleMismatch: The selected speaking role is not assigned to that participant.
messages.validation.inferenceUnconfirmed: An inferred answer must remain unconfirmed until an authorized person verifies it.
messages.validation.resolutionAuthorityRequired: Confirming this premise requires an authorized decision source.
messages.validation.exclusiveChoice: This option cannot be combined with other selections.
messages.validation.noteRequired: Add a short note to explain this selection.
messages.validation.selectionLimit: Reduce the number of selected options.
messages.review.authRuntime: Authentication is in scope, but the selected runtime may require an external or server component.
messages.review.paymentHandling: Payment-related data is in scope. Confirm who processes it and whether the project may store any of it.
messages.review.analyticsPrivacy: Analytics or telemetry is in scope. Recheck the privacy boundary, consent, and prohibited practices.
messages.review.onlineOffline: Online play is selected with an offline-only network policy. Clarify whether this release includes online features.

questions.prompt: What should this release achieve?
questions.help: Choose the milestone whose success you will evaluate.

choices.label: Test the core play with a prototype
An update to an existing game

questions.prompt: What should players primarily experience?
questions.help: Choose the priority when design goals compete; describe the intended feeling in the note.

questions.prompt: What phase is the project in?
questions.help: Preserve existing behavior where the work requires it.

questions.prompt: What is the game concept and genre?
questions.help: Describe what the player does and what makes it distinctive. References are examples, not permission to copy.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: Who are the intended players?
questions.help: Record age range, experience, languages and actual player evidence separately from assumptions.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: Which platforms are in this release?
questions.help: Select committed targets and note minimum devices and operating systems.

questions.prompt: How do players play together?
questions.help: Specify maximum players, local or online play, and whether modes share progress.

questions.prompt: How long is a typical session?
questions.help: Consider interruption, resuming and the total expected play time.

questions.prompt: What actions form the core play loop?
questions.help: Describe action → feedback → next decision, using one concrete example.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: How does play end or succeed?
questions.help: State win, loss, retry and completion conditions; an open-ended game may have none.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: Which progression systems are needed?
questions.help: State limits and reset rules in the note.

questions.prompt: How should difficulty work?
questions.help: Explain fairness, randomness, failure costs and any adaptation boundaries.

questions.prompt: How much playable content is included?
questions.help: Give counts or bounds for stages, characters, items and play time; identify who creates them.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: Which supporting features are required?
questions.help: Select only what must ship in this release.

questions.prompt: What is explicitly out of scope?
questions.help: List tempting additions that must wait; explain what would justify revisiting them.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: What existing work or dependencies must be preserved?
questions.help: Name existing code, formats, tools, assets and compatibility constraints, or state that this is a new project.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: What is the visual direction?
questions.help: Specify camera, readability, references and what should feel distinctive.

questions.prompt: What role does narrative play?
questions.help: Describe setting, tone, branching and localization needs.

questions.prompt: Which audio elements are required?
questions.help: Specify volume controls, subtitles and whether sound may carry essential information.

questions.prompt: Who supplies and approves the assets?
questions.help: Separate placeholders from final assets; record formats, licenses, credits and any generated-asset policy.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: How is the engine or framework chosen?
questions.help: Name fixed tools and versions, or criteria such as team skills, licensing and target platforms.

questions.prompt: Which input methods must work?
questions.help: Specify remapping and whether switching devices during play is supported.

questions.prompt: How is progress saved?
questions.help: Describe save timing, migration, deletion and recovery from interrupted writes.

questions.prompt: What network behavior is required?
questions.help: For online play, define authority, synchronization, disconnection handling, server cost and ownership.

questions.prompt: How do players learn the game?
questions.help: Specify what a first-time player should accomplish without outside help.

questions.prompt: Which accessibility features are required?
questions.help: Confirm needs with intended players; do not assume one setting serves everyone.

questions.prompt: What measurable performance targets must hold?
questions.help: Name test hardware, frame rate, loading time, memory or battery limits and how to measure them.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: What happens when play is interrupted?
questions.help: Cover pause, backgrounding, focus loss, disconnects and return; consider fairness in multiplayer.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: What content or interactions must be avoided?
questions.help: Record audience and rating expectations, sensitive content limits, chat moderation and reporting where relevant.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: What monetization is planned?
questions.help: Specify purchase boundaries and prohibited pressure; leave undecided details visibly open.

questions.prompt: Which player data is collected or shared?
questions.help: Identify purpose, storage, retention, deletion and service operators; local save data also needs a boundary.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: What rights and distribution constraints apply?
questions.help: List asset and engine licenses, attribution, ownership, platform requirements and who verifies them.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: What people, time and budget are available?
questions.help: Name responsibilities, skills, milestones and a contingency for missing capacity.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: How will players receive the game?
questions.help: Name channels, release ownership and any account or review requirements.

questions.prompt: What must be handed over with the game?
questions.help: Specify reproducible builds, source, editable assets, licenses, test evidence and operation instructions.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: Who handles updates and incidents after release?
questions.help: Define ownership, support duration, compatibility, rollback and service shutdown expectations.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: How will the intended experience be tested?
questions.help: Define participants, scenarios, observations and revision criteria; separate opinions from measured behavior.
questions.placeholder: Describe the premise, limits and evidence. You may leave it unresolved.

questions.prompt: Which scenarios must pass before release?
questions.help: Add concrete steps and expected results in the note.

questions.prompt: Who decides the game is ready, using what criteria?
questions.help: Name the decision role, acceptable defects and measurable release gates.

questions.prompt: How should unresolved design decisions be handled?
questions.help: State delegated boundaries and when work should stop for renewed alignment.
